newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to watch Masters golf tournament on TV.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to watch Masters golf tournament on TV.

text.p: President Clinton gave an enthusiastic thumbs-up Sunday when asked if he would watch the Masters golf tournament that 21-year-old prodigy Tiger Woods appeared poised to win.

Clinton, whose own golf game was on hold until at least the end of the summer because of a knee injury, attended church on Sunday and responded to a reporter's question about whether he would watch the Masters with a silent thumbs-up.
He did not reply when asked if he had finished his taxes, which, like those of most U.S. citizens, are due on Tuesday.

Clinton tore a tendon in his right leg when he stumbled on a step after midnight on March 14 at the Florida home of golf pro Greg Norman and was rushed to Washington for emergency surgery, missing a golf tournament he had planned to play.

The injury is expected to keep him on crutches for about another month and he will then face several more months of physical therapy, putting him by his own estimate at least four months and a few weeks from any return to the links.

Woods, playing his only third Masters and his first as a professional, led the tournament at Georgia's Augusta National golf course by a record nine strokes after three rounds. On Saturday he shot a flawless seven-under-par 65 to tie the Masters 54-hole scoring record.
